subject: Lumina POC — auth choices, tool-call fallback & error handling plan
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Liam Park <liam.park@luminahealth.com>, Nadia Reyes <n.reyes@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>

Subject: Lumina POC — auth choices, tool-call fallback & error handling plan

Hi Liam / Nadia — thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick follow-up with a concise plan so we can align engineering and pick an MVP approach for the POC. TL;DR: two auth paths (API key vs OAuth), recommend hybrid routing + parallel tool-call with ranked fallback, and a minimal structured-output schema for the first demo.

Summary of requirements we captured on the call:
- Query routing: US region preferred; multi-region failover if cross-region latency >120ms.
- Data flow: user prompt -> Redwood hosted inference -> optional tool calls (patient lookup, eligibility check, external API) -> structured JSON response to your app.
- Auth constraints: Lumina cannot share long-lived user credentials; security team prefers per-session short-lived tokens or OAuth.
- Quality need: relevance for triage prompts; we discussed embeddings + lightweight reranker to improve top-3 results.

Our recommended POC approach (MVP):
1) Auth: implement OAuth for user-scoped actions (patient lookup), API-key for server-to-server calls (background enrichment). We'll provide a sample OAuth flow and short-lived token guidance.
2) SDK + integration: use Redwood JS SDK (snippet attached) with plugin-style tool manifest (sample_tool_manifest.json attached). SDK will handle KV cache for embedding lookups and manage retries for tool calls.
3) Tool calling: run tool calls in parallel when independent (e.g., demographic enrichment + benefits check) and in sequence when dependent (lookup -> eligibility). Use an orchestration policy that prefers parallelism but limits concurrency (max 3 parallel) to control egress.
4) Error handling / fallbacks:
   - If a tool call times out (>=2s), fall back to a cached response if available; otherwise return a graceful partial result with a status field indicating degraded data.
   - If primary tool fails (5xx), attempt a secondary provider (we can demo a cheap 3rd-party fallback).
   - Model-level fallback: if structured output validation fails, return an error code with suggested corrective prompt to the UI so the app can re-run with the adjusted schema.
5) Embeddings & reranker: index triage prompts in Pinecone / Redis vector store; run a lightweight reranker (cross-encoder) on top-5 candidates to present best 3.

Attachments: lumina_integration_guide.pdf (arch + SDK snippets), auth_flow.png (OAuth vs API key diagram), sample_tool_manifest.json (tool definitions and idempotency hints).

Next steps / asks:
- Can your security team confirm they can accept OAuth redirect URIs for the POC?
- Are you comfortable with us using a temporary Pinecone demo index, or do you prefer we set up a dummy Redis instance in your AWS account?
- Agree to a 2-week POC cadence: week 1 integrate SDK + auth, week 2 tool calls + reranker demo.

I’ll loop in Aditya (SE) for a short technical follow-up and a 30-minute run-through of the sample manifest. If that works, how’s Thursday 11:00 PT for a pairing session?

Thanks,

Thanks Vanessa — this is super helpful and aligns with what we discussed. A few quick clarifications from our side:
- Security: we can do OAuth for user-scoped calls. Our IdP team will need the redirect URI; they prefer the token TTL to be <= 1 hour for demo accounts.
- Vector store: for speed, we'd rather stand up a small Redis vector DB in our AWS account (we have a test VPC) — that should be straightforward for week 1.
- Tool independence: patient lookup must be first (sensitive PII), others can be parallelized after the lookup completes. Can Redwood's SDK keep the patient id cached for that user session?

Regarding the fallback: Can you outline the UX shape when a tool is degraded? We want the app to show a clear indicator so clinicians know which info is provisional.

We can do Thursday 11:00 PT — I'll invite our eng lead, Nadia.

—Liam

Subject: Re: Lumina POC — auth choices, tool-call fallback & error handling plan

Great questions — quick technical notes and a tiny SDK snippet inline. Yes, the Redwood JS SDK supports per-session KV cached values (session-scoped) so we can store patient_id for the duration of the session and automatically attach it to subsequent tool calls.

Example (pseudo-code):
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY, region: 'us' });
await client.auth.startOAuth({ provider: 'oidc-lumina', redirectUri: 'https://lumina-prod.test/redirect' });
// after oauth success
client.session.set('patient_id', 'patient-123');

// tool call orchestration: run independent tools in parallel, dependent tools sequentially
const results = await client.tools.runMany([
  { id: 'demographics', independent: true },
  { id: 'payerCheck', independent: true },
  { id: 'eligibility', dependsOn: ['demographics'] }
], { parallelLimit: 3, timeoutMs: 2000 });

Error handling built into runMany returns structured metadata: { success: boolean, toolResponses: [...], partial: boolean, errors: [...] }
We include idempotency tokens in manifest and suggest a retry/backoff that escalates to fallback provider after 2 failed attempts. For the UI: each tool response includes a status enum (OK | PARTIAL | ERROR) and a reason string; we can surface PARTIAL with a tooltip that explains the data may be cached or from the fallback provider.

Attachments in the email bundle include the sample tool manifest that shows:
- tool id, name, input schema, output schema, isIdempotent, fallbackProviderId, slaHints
- suggestion to mark PII-returning tools as "sensitive" so SDK enforces stricter logging redaction.

I'll bring a debug-run playbook to the Thursday pairing session to walk through a simulated timeout and show the SDK's retry/fallback behaviour.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
